title: Artificial Intelligence in Placental Pathology: From Spatial Analytics to Molecular Proxies
content: The placenta is a crucial determinant of the success of pregnancy. However, manual evaluation of its pathology is limited by poor reproducibility and a global shortage of specialized perinatal pathologists. Besides, predicting recurrent pregnancy complications remains highly challenging, which severely limits the timely deployment of proactive therapeutic interventions. Automated artificial intelligence screening of the delivered placenta will help to overcome these bottlenecks. In this work, we synthesize the transition toward self-supervised Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) that yield robust, stain-agnostic tissue embeddings. Furthermore, we evaluate the emergence of Non-Euclidean Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) that map cellular topologies to quantify mal-perfusion, alongside multimodal generative cross-attention networks (MGCN) that integrate gigapixel histology with electronic medical records (EMR) to improve pregnancy risk stratification. Moreover, we propose a novel, functional systems-biology framework to retroactively bridge digital morphometrics – such as impaired trophoblast fusion and invasion – to upstream dysregulated molecular cascades, including the ERK1/2–DUSP, FAK–MAPK, and HIF-1α regulatory axes. Finally, we address translational bottlenecks – such as diagnostic inter-observer variation, systemic clinical confounders, and geographic data bias – and outline hardware edge-deployment strategies for the pathology floor. Ultimately, automated placental screening will help to reveal immediate newborn developmental risks and maternal pathological recurrence risks across subsequent pregnancies. Together, these computational paradigms offer a potential translational roadmap to standardize digital placental pathology into a personalized reproductive medicine pillar.
